question: Researchers pressure-tested running shoes from three brands at three prices. How did the cheapest pairs cushion the foot?
answer: As well or better. Clinghan and colleagues measured pressure under the foot in low, medium and high-priced models of three brands, while walking and running on a treadmill. The cheaper shoes cushioned at least as well, and comfort did not follow price either. Whatever the extra money bought, it was not cushioning.
move: Test what the price claims to buy before paying for it.
ask: What did I last pay extra for without checking whether it does the job any better?
trap: Assuming a higher price buys better protection for the foot.
source: Clinghan et al., Br J Sports Med, 2008
reference: Clinghan et al., Do you get value for money when you buy an expensive pair of running shoes?, British Journal of Sports Medicine, 2008
